visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 accurately shows the archer, launch angle, velocity components, parabolic path, and vertical-motion equation in context, while Lesson 2 mostly shows an empty Desmos grid with warning icons/undefined theta and no visible projectile trajectory or range representation.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 has a well-formed, wired fill-in gate after act_introduction with a real prompt, accepted answers, hint, and remediation path, while Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning checkpoints.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 has clear, natural narration with well-paced explanatory phrasing and no obvious spoken-text defects, while Lesson 2 contains repetition, awkward instructional phrasing, and an abrupt unrelated ending ('A golfer hits a ball.') that makes the narration feel defective.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 at least includes timed cues that mostly occur near the narration's visual references, while Lesson 2 has no beat/cue timing data despite referencing visual actions like showing the arc and clicking the endpoint, making its synchronization unsupported and worse.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 1 correctly builds the range solution through velocity decomposition, vertical flight time, and constant horizontal motion, whereas Lesson 2 mostly has the learner plot/click a calculator trajectory with little derivation or conceptual explanation and an irrelevant transcript artifact at the end.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 has a cleaner, more consistent full-frame presentation with centered readable title text, while Lesson 2 is heavily cluttered by browser chrome, chat widgets, playback controls, and overlapping interface elements that make the lesson feel off-center and visually noisy despite some legible text.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents strongly prefer Lesson 1, with high confidences across visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, conceptual accuracy, and polish. Lesson 1 is described as visually accurate, interactive, well narrated, reasonably synchronized, conceptually sound, and polished. Lesson 2 is consistently criticized for missing or broken visuals, lack of functioning checkpoints, awkward narration artifacts, unsupported synchronization, weaker conceptual derivation, and cluttered presentation. The verdict is unanimous with no meaningful split, so Lesson 1 is the clear winner.
